title: What is a Liquidity Sweep?
summary: A liquidity sweep occurs when price moves past a known high or low to trigger stop losses before reversing.
content: Institutions need large amounts of liquidity to fill their orders. By pushing price into a zone where retail stop-losses are clustered (e.g., above a previous daily high), they create a surge of sell orders they can buy into, which then fuels the move in the opposite direction.

title: Fair Value Gaps (FVG)
summary: An imbalance in price action where only one side of the market (buyers or sellers) is present.
content: A FVG is a three-candle sequence where the first and third candles do not overlap, leaving a gap in the middle. Markets have a mathematical tendency to return to these gaps to provide liquidity and balance the price action.

title: Order Blocks (OB)
summary: The footprints of institutional buying or selling.
content: An order block is the last opposite-colored candle before a strong move that breaks market structure. It represents where institutions placed their large orders, and price often returns to these zones to pick up remaining orders.
